title: Discharging the toolkit's standing independence hypothesis
content: The measure-theoretic OQ-01 program built a modular toolkit whose lemmas each assume, as a hypothesis, that a bad event $A_i$ is independent of the joint avoidance of some other events: $\mathrm{IndepSet}\,(A_i)\,\bigl(\bigcap_{j\in S}(A_j)^c\bigr)\,\mu$. For example `seq_indep_avoidance_eq_prod` assumes $\forall n,\ \mathrm{IndepSet}\,(A_n)\,(\bigcap_{j<n}(A_j)^c)\,\mu$ and `cond_failure_eq_measure_of_indep_subset` assumes it for a subset $S$. Those docstrings observe that this is 'a strictly weaker, one-sided condition that mutual independence implies' — but that implication was never actually proved in Lean. This file proves it: from full mutual independence $\mathrm{iIndepSet}\,A\,\mu$ and $i\notin S$, it derives $\mathrm{IndepSet}\,(A_i)\,(\bigcap_{j\in S}(A_j)^c)\,\mu$, so the whole development is grounded in a single hypothesis.
mathContext: Bridge from family mutual independence iIndepSet A μ to pairwise independence IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ) μ, for i ∉ S over an arbitrary index type ι. This is the d=0 (fully-independent) case of the LLL's non-neighbour reduction: every other event is a non-neighbour, so conditioning on their avoidance cannot change A i.

title: Measure factorization via σ-algebra independence of disjoint index sets
content: `indep_avoidance` proves $\mu\bigl(A_i\cap\bigcap_{j\in S}(A_j)^c\bigr)=\mu(A_i)\cdot\mu\bigl(\bigcap_{j\in S}(A_j)^c\bigr)$ for $i\notin S$. The engine is Mathlib's `iIndepSet.indep_generateFrom_of_disjoint`: for disjoint index sets it makes the generated σ-algebras independent. Applied to the singleton $\{i\}$ and the finite set $\uparrow S$ (disjoint since $i\notin S$), it yields $\mathrm{Indep}\,(\mathrm{generateFrom}\,\{A_i\})\,(\mathrm{generateFrom}\,\{A_k:k\in S\})\,\mu$. Then $A_i$ is measurable in the first σ-algebra (`measurableSet_generateFrom` on the singleton), and $\bigcap_{j\in S}(A_j)^c$ is measurable in the second (each $(A_j)^c$ is a generator complement, and `Finset.measurableSet_biInter` closes the finite intersection). `Indep_iff` turns the σ-algebra independence into the intersection-measure identity.
mathContext: The finite avoidance ⋂_{j∈S} (A j)ᶜ lives in generateFrom {A k : k∈S} because it is a finite intersection of complements of generators — this is what lets the two-σ-algebra independence apply to it. Indep_iff : Indep m₁ m₂ μ ↔ ∀ t₁ t₂, MeasurableSet[m₁] t₁ → MeasurableSet[m₂] t₂ → μ(t₁ ∩ t₂) = μ t₁ * μ t₂.
relatedConcepts: generated σ-algebras of disjoint index sets
measure factorization μ(s ∩ t) = μ s · μ t

title: The bridge: mutual independence ⟹ pairwise IndepSet
content: `indepSet_avoidance` (flagship) repackages the measure factorization as the term the toolkit actually consumes: $\mathrm{IndepSet}\,(A_i)\,\bigl(\bigcap_{j\in S}(A_j)^c\bigr)\,\mu$. Since `iIndepSet A μ` yields `IsProbabilityMeasure μ` (hence `IsZeroOrProbabilityMeasure`), the characterization `indepSet_iff_measure_inter_eq_mul` reduces the `IndepSet` goal to exactly the identity $\mu(A_i\cap H)=\mu(A_i)\cdot\mu(H)$ that `indep_avoidance` supplies. This one lemma retroactively grounds every hypothesis-carrying lemma of the OQ-01 program in mutual independence: `seq_indep_avoidance_eq_prod`, `cond_failure_eq_measure_of_indep_subset`, and their downstream consequences can now be instantiated directly from `iIndepSet A μ`.
mathContext: IndepSet s t μ ↔ μ (s ∩ t) = μ s * μ t requires [IsZeroOrProbabilityMeasure μ]; here μ is a probability measure by iIndepSet.isProbabilityMeasure. The lemma holds for ANY index subset S disjoint from {i} — in the d=0 regime there are no dependency neighbours to exclude, so S can be all other events.
relatedConcepts: grounding the toolkit in mutual independence

title: Conditional corollary: conditioning on independent avoidance preserves probability
content:
`cond_avoidance_eq_self` proves $\mu[A_i\mid  igcap_{j\in S}(A_j)^c]=\mu(A_i)$ for $i
otin S$, whenever the avoidance $H= igcap_{j\in S}(A_j)^c$ has positive measure. `cond_apply'` unfolds the conditional as $(\mu H)^{-1}\cdot\mu(H\cap A_i)$; after `Set.inter_comm` and the factorization `indep_avoidance`, the goal is $(\mu H)^{-1}\cdot(\mu(A_i)\cdot\mu H)$, and `ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel` (using $\mu H
eq 0$ and $\mu H
eq\infty$, the latter from the probability measure) collapses it to $\mu(A_i)$. This is precisely `cond_failure_eq_measure_of_indep_subset` from the dependency-split toolkit, now with its `IndepSet` hypothesis discharged — the $d=0$ non-neighbour step of the LLL induction, direct from mutual independence.
mathContext: cond_apply' (ht : MeasurableSet t) : μ[t|s] = (μ s)⁻¹ * μ (s ∩ t). The positivity hypothesis μ H ≠ 0 is automatic in the LLL (the base case proves μ(⋂ Aⱼᶜ) > 0 under μ(Aⱼ) < 1) but is kept explicit here to keep the bridge independent of any positivity route.

title: Chain-rule prefix specialization: bₖ collapses to μ(Aₖ)
content: `cond_prefix_eq_self` specialises the subset $S$ to the strictly-earlier indices $\{j : j<k\}$ over a `LinearOrder ι`; then $k\notin S$ follows from `lt_irrefl`, and `cond_avoidance_eq_self` gives $\mu[A_k\mid \bigcap_{j<k}(A_j)^c]=\mu(A_k)$. This is exactly the per-event conditional failure probability $b_k$ that the chain-rule scaffold consumes: in the independent regime $b_k=\mu(A_k)$, so the quantitative avoidance bound $\prod_k(1-b_k)$ recovers the exact base-case factorization $\prod_k(1-\mu(A_k))$ — now derived from `iIndepSet A μ` alone, tying the chain-rule and base-case sub-programs together on their common ground.
mathContext: Connects to lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01-chain-rule (avoidance_eq_prod_survival_cond) and the base case lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01 (lll_independent_meas_iInter_compl). The full bounded-dependency-degree LLL — deriving bₖ ≤ xₖ across a dependency graph under e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1 — remains the open OQ-01 target.
prerequisites: LinearOrder on the index type, lt_irrefl
